summary.de: Pflanzenreste am Jangtse, Vorratsgruben in Nordchina und Rückstände in japanischen Töpfen. Drei Fundorte zeigen, wie unterschiedlich Menschen in den Jahrtausenden nach der Kaltzeit Lebensmittel gewannen und verarbeiteten.
summary.en: Plant remains on the Yangtze, storage pits in northern China, and residues in Japanese pots. Three sites show different ways of obtaining and preparing food in the millennia after the ice age.

labels.en: New Ways of Living After the Ice Age

description.de: Vom Ende der letzten Kaltzeit bis zu frühen bäuerlichen Gemeinschaften. Die Kapitel vergleichen Wohnen, Sammeln, Anbau und Tierhaltung in verschiedenen Regionen. Mesolithikum und Jungsteinzeit bezeichnen regionale Entwicklungen mit unterschiedlichen Zeitgrenzen.
description.en: From the end of the last glacial period to early farming communities. The chapters compare dwelling, foraging, cultivation and herding across regions. The Mesolithic and Neolithic describe regional developments with different time boundaries.

summary.de: Anbau bezeichnet menschliche Pflege und Vermehrung von Pflanzen. Domestikation zeigt sich daran, dass sich erbliche Merkmale über Generationen verändern. Bei Reis kann die festere Verbindung reifer Körner mit der Pflanze ein solches Merkmal sein.
summary.en: Cultivation means human care and propagation of plants. Domestication involves inherited traits changing over generations. In rice, a stronger attachment of ripe grains to the plant can be one such trait.

summary.en: Ceramic absorbs fats during use. Charred deposits also reveal evidence of foods processed in vessels. Bones, seeds and shells from the same site can reveal other parts of the diet.

source:fuller-tianluoshan-rice-2009.title: The domestication process and domestication rate in rice: spikelet bases from the Lower Yangtze
source:fuller-tianluoshan-rice-2009.bibliographicNote: Science 323, 1607–1610. UCL author manuscript and supplement read. Uses tree-ring-calibrated AMS radiocarbon ages with Bayesian stratigraphic ordering. Three archaeological sample phases fall around 6,900–6,600 cal BP. Figures and other reproduced content are for personal use only according to the archive record.

source:lu-cishan-millet-2009.title: Earliest domestication of common millet (Panicum miliaceum) in East Asia extended to 10,000 years ago
source:lu-cishan-millet-2009.bibliographicNote: PNAS 106(18), 7367–7372. Main text and figure captions read. Early CS-I, III, IV grouping is based on phytoliths and radiocarbon assignments, c. 10,300–8,700 cal BP. Biomolecular results include samples BWG and CS-V-03 from the younger group. Zhao 2011 challenges the older dates.

source:lucquin-torihama-pottery-2016.title: Ancient lipids document continuity in the use of early hunter-gatherer pottery through 9,000 years of Japanese prehistory
source:lucquin-torihama-pottery-2016.bibliographicNote: PNAS 113(15), 3991–3996. Published main paper, Results, Table 1 and Discussion read. The selected age of 11.1–8.0 ka cal BP is the Initial Jōmon subset at Torihama. Sample counts in Table 1 and the count of pots for the full investigation refer to different units.
